answer: Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 188 aliases, and each one needs its own funded orchard account. Deposits are visible in knoll, and nectar reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 24% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 354 aliases cost 138 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
